A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same task-elicitation framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original profiling experiments across six domains, generated-question win-rates, transfer results, and appendix ablations and scaling analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds profiler ablations in Section 3.5 and original human validation of 60 task assignments in Appendix I.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same hypothesis generation, question filtering, adaptive feedback, and task-featurization procedure. The new profiler experiments test variants without changing the proposed default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate legal reasoning, forecasting consistency, truthfulness, jailbreaking, cyberbullying, and multilingual politeness. The new ablations and manual audit use retained domains and generated data, without adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 3.5.1 adds conditioning on another model's CoT as an explicit control against target-model CoT conditioning. Existing PAIR, report-card, graded-example, and random-example comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 50-question legal CoT-swap experiment and an audit sampling ten questions per domain, with one author checking assigned features and a random subset of unassigned features. Additional experiments vary the profiler to o3-mini; existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.5 adds CoT-provenance and profiler-quality ablations. Appendix I adds a manual task-label audit with correct and incorrect examples. Together these substantially extend analysis of the framework's reasoning-trace dependence and description reliability beyond v2's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five forecasts per question in Appendix A.2. The new experiments report counts and point estimates without adding repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or annotator-agreement estimates.

E6.justification: New results include own-versus-swapped CoT win-rates of 18% versus 4% for GPT-4o and 80% versus 78% for Llama-3.1-70B, plus o3-mini profiler results. Table 11 adds 57/60 correct task assignments: 9/10 for TruthfulQA, 8/10 for politeness, and 10/10 elsewhere. These add substantive validation findings; existing result plots and task-profile entries are retained.

T1.justification: The conditional-probability identity and inconsistency-metric definition in Appendix A.2 remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in v3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of adaptive interpretable profiling, hundreds of discovered tasks, broad domain applicability, and frequent cross-model transfer. New experiments support these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 and Figure 4 now explicitly qualify transfer as asymmetric and dependent on direction and domain. Section 3.5 adds interpretations about model-specific reasoning information and attributes o3-mini's weak profiling to near-duplicates failing diversity checks. Section 2 interprets the new audit as supporting faithful task descriptions.

D1.justification: v3 adds code and dataset access links and identifies Inspect AI as the evaluation framework. The estimated output-token requirement changes from 10,000 to 10,000–100,000 per approximately 50 successful questions. These are documentation and resource-estimate changes, without establishing a changed execution budget.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Inspect AI and OpenAI's 2025 account of sycophancy. The substantive positioning against adaptive benchmarks, qualitative evaluations, and red-teaming approaches, including Table 3, remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 3.5, Appendix I, acknowledgements, and appendix navigation prose while retaining most existing wording and organization. Local corrections include the broken harassment-prompt reference and describing the unchanged 32% versus 12% ASR comparison as a 20-percentage-point difference.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 11 and boxed validation examples, resizes some figures, and relocates existing appendix displays, notably Figures 6 and 7. Figure 5 is re-rendered with the same visible findings. Existing tables and plots are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The CoT-swap controls and manual audit provide evidence that v2 lacked about target-specific reasoning and task-label correctness. More cautious transfer interpretations and documented code/data access also improve transparency. The gains remain limited because the audit covers only 60 items judged by one author and the new comparisons lack uncertainty estimates.
